newsitem.title: USA: Asia Pulp buys 64 pct of Nippecraft.
newsitem.headline: Asia Pulp buys 64 pct of Nippecraft.

text.p: Asia Pulp & Paper Co Ltd said Wednesday its unit APP Printing (Holding) Pte Ltd has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a 64 percent stake in Nippecraft Ltd for about US$32 million.
In an announcement from its headquarters in Singapore, Asia Pulp said the stake would be purchased from Nippecraft's controlling shareholder.
Nippecraft is a Singapore company that produces stationery and related products.

Asia Pulp said its unit is required under Singapore law to make a general offer for the remaining shares of the issued share capital of Nippecraft at the same price on the per share basis as that paid to Nippecraft's controlling shareholder.
An Asia Pulp spokeswoman in New York declined to identify the shareholder.

In addition, its unit has agreed to subscribe, for US$6.4 million, to a proposed rights offering by Nippecraft. If the rights offering does not proceed, Asia Pulp said it has agreed to extend a subordinated shareholder's loan of up to US$10 million.
Asia Pulp also announced it has acquired a 30 percent stake in PT Toko Gunung Anung, an owner and operator of 38 retail outlets in Indonesia that primarily sells books and stationery products.
The purchase price was not disclosed.
Purchase of the stakes in the two companies was part of its strategy to vertically integrate into high value added paper and packaging products, Asia Pulp said.
Asia Pulp, one of the world's largest pulp and paper comnpanies, has 15 manufacturing plants in Indonesia and China and sells its products in more than 50 countries.
